name: AYN Odin 2
summary: AYN's Android-based handheld (Qualcomm SM8550). ROCKNIX (mainline Linux) publishes a build; KNULLI's supported-device table does not list it (checked 2026-10-29).

variants.notes: Android-based AYN handheld. ROCKNIX lists Base / Pro / Max (SM8550) on its device page; not listed in KNULLI's supported-device table (checked 2026-10-29).

homebrew.name: ROCKNIX
homebrew.firmware: SD card image (SM8550 build); ROCKNIX ABL boot-mode switch.
homebrew.summary: Mainline-Linux retro gaming OS (Sway + Emulation Station) for the AYN Odin 2. Image is written to an SD card; internal installation is optional.

compatibility.note: ROCKNIX lists the AYN Odin 2 (Base / Pro / Max, Qualcomm 8gen2 SM8550) with a mainline Linux kernel and Freedreno/Turnip graphics. The device page states no stability or status rating and no model limits beyond Base / Pro / Max. The ROCKNIX ABL steps are 'only required if your device doesn't have a fastboot menu to switch the Boot Mode'; the page does not say which units already have one, so whether the ABL flash is needed is unclear. ROCKNIX does not state a bootloader-unlock requirement on this page.

requirements: A computer with an SD card reader and an image writer (Rufus, Raspberry Pi Imager or dd).
Possibly the ROCKNIX ABL (flashed from Android as root with backup_abl.sh then flash_abl.sh) if the unit has no fastboot boot-mode menu; the page does not say which units need it.
warnings: Flashing the ROCKNIX ABL replaces the device's ABL; run backup_abl.sh first, as the page instructs.
installtointernal (optional) resets Android userdata, like a factory reset.

homebrew.name: Batocera.linux
homebrew.firmware: SD card image (Batocera 43.1 handheld build); written to an SD card.
homebrew.summary: Batocera.linux's own handheld build, the upstream project ROCKNIX and KNULLI derive from. Written to an SD card.

compatibility.note: Batocera 43.1's handheld download list names 'Odin 2' (alongside Odin 2 Mini and Odin 2 Portal, which are not models in this record). The page gives the download only, not install steps.

requirements: A device from Batocera's handheld download list.
A computer with an SD card reader and an image writer.
warnings: Batocera publishes a separate image per device; check the exact row before writing.
